html:
The Capanahua are a small Indigenous people of the Peruvian Amazon, living on the Tapiche and Buncuya rivers in the Loreto region of Peru. They speak one of the Panoan languages, related to those of the Shipibo-Konibo and the Matsés.

They were hit by the rubber boom around 1900, and later many married Spanish-speaking settlers. Of about 400 Capanahua, only around fifty still speak the language.
